Saturday Night Live is spending Halloween night in Studio 8H — and it is handing the stage to a first-time host straight out of this year's biggest horror hit. Inde Navarrette hosts the fourth episode of season 52 on Saturday, October 31, with Gracie Abrams returning as musical guest.

The episode airs live coast-to-coast at 11:30 p.m. ET / 10:30 p.m. CT / 8:30 p.m. PT on NBC and Peacock, and it will be available to stream on Peacock starting Sunday. The show is coming off a brief early-season hiatus, with three episodes of season 52 already aired.

Navarrette is the breakout star of the 2026 horror blockbuster Obsession, playing Nikki Freeman opposite Michael Johnston's Bear Bailey. According to NBC, the film earned more than $263 million in theaters domestically and more than $523 million worldwide, and Navarrette's Nikki became so iconic that the character was added to the cast of Halloween Horror Nights at Universal Studios Hollywood for the 2026 season. That makes her a fitting choice for one of the rare Halloween-night episodes in the show's history — a short list that, per the Journal News, includes Catherine O'Hara in 1992 and John Mulaney in 2020.

Abrams is back for her second turn as musical guest, following her debut in season 50 on December 14, 2024, when she performed "That's So True" and "I Love You, I'm Sorry" on the Chris Rock-hosted show. She released her third studio album, Daughter from Hell, on July 17, 2026; its lead single, "Hit the Wall," peaked at No. 26 on the Billboard Hot 100 and spent 20 weeks on the chart. Her Look at My Life Tour begins in Denver on December 2 and wraps with back-to-back shows in Barcelona, Spain, on May 27 and 28, 2027.

Analysis: A Horror Star Meets a Halloween Institution

The booking is a neat piece of scheduling: a performer whose breakout role is already part of Halloween Horror Nights hosting on the one night of the year when sketch comedy and horror naturally overlap. For Navarrette, the test is whether the screen presence that carried a horror hit translates to live sketch, where timing is unforgiving and there is no second take. For Abrams, the return slot is a showcase for a new album cycle just weeks before a world tour — the kind of appearance that can turn a single into a set-list staple. Either way, a Halloween-night episode is a rare stage, and both performers arrive with momentum behind them.
